propositions: The review-bot uvicorn app logs the full request line including query parameters to stderr/journald, exposing the authentication token from ?token=... in plaintext on every /webhook and /rerun request
The webhook_token is derived from GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN, a Gerrit credential, so exposure of the token via logs allows an attacker to drive reviews and act against Gerrit
The logged secret is discoverable by journal greps, log-sharing in tickets and chat, and future log-shipping, making the blast radius wider than the container itself
The exposure is fail-open with no error signal, so it remains undetected during normal operation and only surfaces when logs are actively searched or shared

The fix relocates the token from the query string to the X-Rebar-Token HTTP header (which uvicorn access logs do not record) with a redaction filter as backstop, and requires token rotation to treat already-leaked material as compromised
